t.2.4.1: Then, when the citizens had departed, the king consulted once more with his ministers, and thereupon he, who knew how to reach a resolve, made his decision.
t.2.4.2: "Tomorrow indeed the Puṣya constellation will be in the ascendant; tomorrow my son Rāma, whose eyes are coppery like the lotus, should be consecrated as heir apparent," so the lord resolved.
t.2.4.3: Then King Daśaratha, having entered the inner apartments, commanded the charioteer: "Bring Rāma here again."
t.2.4.4: Accepting those words, the charioteer went back quickly to Rāma's residence to bring Rāma once more.
t.2.4.5: His arrival was announced once more to Rāma by the doorkeepers, and as soon as he heard that he had come, Rāma was filled with apprehension.
t.2.4.6: Having quickly had him brought in, Rāma spoke these words: "Tell me again, in full, whatever is the purpose of your coming."
t.2.4.8: Having heard these words of the charioteer, Rāma, filled with haste, then set out for the royal palace to see the lord of men once again.
t.2.4.7: Then the charioteer said to him: "The king wishes to see you. Having heard this, you are the authority here, whether for going or for doing otherwise."
t.2.4.10: And even as he was entering his father's palace, the glorious Rāghava saw his father from afar, and, with palms joined in reverence, he bowed down before him.
t.2.4.11: Raising him up as he bowed low, the king embraced him, and, pointing him to a splendid seat, spoke to him once more.
t.2.4.9: Hearing that Rāma had arrived, King Daśaratha, wishing to be alone with him, had his dear and most excellent son brought into the palace.
t.2.4.12: Rāma, I am old and have lived a long life; I have enjoyed the pleasures I desired, and I have likewise performed hundreds of sacrifices rich in food and abundant in gifts to the priests.
t.2.4.13: A cherished offspring has been born to me: you, who are today without equal on earth. I have given gifts, performed sacrifices, and studied the scriptures, O best of men.
t.2.4.14: O hero, I have enjoyed the pleasures I desired, and I am free of my debt to the gods, the seers, the ancestors and the brahmins, and likewise to myself.
t.2.4.15: Nothing remains for me to do except your consecration. Therefore you ought to do for me whatever I may tell you.
t.2.4.16: Today all the subjects desire you as their ruler; therefore, my dear son, I shall consecrate you as heir apparent.
t.2.4.17: Moreover, Rāma, I see dreadful dreams of the most inauspicious kind, and great meteors fall here with thunderclaps and mighty roars.
t.2.4.18: And the astrologers tell me, Rāma, that my birth-star is beset by fierce planets: the Sun, Mars and Rāhu.
t.2.4.19: For generally, when such omens arise, a king either meets his death or falls into some terrible calamity.
t.2.4.20: Therefore, Rāghava, while my mind is still not clouded, have yourself consecrated, for the minds of living beings are fickle.
t.2.4.21: Today the moon has entered Punarvasu, which comes just before Puṣya; tomorrow, the astrologers will declare, the conjunction with Puṣya is certain.
t.2.4.23: Therefore this night must be spent by you today in fasting together with your bride, observing your vow, with your self restrained, lying upon a bed of darbha grass.
t.2.4.22: Then, under the constellation Puṣya, let yourself be consecrated, for my mind seems to urge me to haste. Tomorrow I shall consecrate you in the office of heir apparent, O scorcher of foes.
t.2.4.24: And let your friends, ever vigilant, guard you on every side today, for undertakings of this kind are beset by many obstacles.
t.2.4.25: And just so long as Bharata is away, gone from this city, for just that long, in my view, the time for your consecration has come.
t.2.4.26: Granted, your brother Bharata abides in the conduct of the virtuous; he follows his elder brother, is righteous in spirit, compassionate, and has mastered his senses.
t.2.4.28: Thus addressed, and given leave with the words "Go," with the consecration to take place on the morrow, Rāma saluted his father and went to his house.
t.2.4.27: But it is my belief, O Rāghava, that the minds of men are inconstant, even the minds of the virtuous who are ever steadfast in dharma and shine with the good deeds they have done.
t.2.4.29: Having entered his own dwelling, and the consecration having been appointed by the king, he went out at that very moment and went to his mother's inner apartments.
t.2.4.30: There in the shrine he saw his mother, wholly devoted, clad in linen and keeping silence, praying for good fortune.
t.2.4.31: Sumitrā had already come there beforehand, and Lakṣmaṇa likewise, and Sītā had been sent for, having heard the welcome news of Rāma's consecration.
t.2.4.32: At that time Kausalyā was sitting with her eyes half-closed, attended by Sumitrā, Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa.
t.2.4.33: Having heard of her son's consecration as heir apparent under the constellation Puṣya, she, through control of the breath, was meditating upon the Supreme Person, Janārdana.
t.2.4.34: Approaching her as she sat thus intent on her religious observances, and saluting her, Rāma then spoke these words to her, gladdening her heart.
t.2.4.35: Mother, I have been appointed by my father to the task of protecting the people. Tomorrow my consecration will take place, as my father has commanded me.
t.2.4.36: "This night must be spent in fasting by Sītā too, together with me": so my father spoke to me in the presence of the officiating priests and preceptors.
t.2.4.37: Whatever auspicious rites are fitting here for the consecration that is to take place tomorrow, have them performed today for me and for Vaidehī as well.
t.2.4.39: My child Rāma, live long; may your enemies be slain. Endowed with prosperity, bring joy to my kinsmen and to those of Sumitrā.
t.2.4.38: Hearing this, which she had long yearned for, Kausalyā spoke these words to Rāma, her voice soft and faltering with tears of joy.
t.2.4.40: Ah, my dear son, under an auspicious star were you born of me, you by whom your father Daśaratha has been won over through your virtues.
t.2.4.41: Ah, not in vain has been my patient devotion to the lotus-eyed Puruṣa, since this royal splendor of the Ikṣvāku kingdom will now come to rest upon you, my son.
t.2.4.42: Thus addressed by his mother, Rāma, as if smiling, looked at the Bhārata who sat bowing low with joined palms and spoke these words to him.
t.2.4.43: Lakṣmaṇa, rule this earth together with me. This royal fortune has come to you as well, for you are my second inner self.
t.2.4.44: O Saumitri, enjoy the pleasures you desire and the fruits of kingship, for it is for your sake that I desire both life and the kingdom.
t.2.4.45: Having spoken thus to Lakṣmaṇa, Rāma saluted his two mothers, and, having had Sītā take her leave as well, he went to his own residence.
